Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Mujadila (The Woman Who Pleads), because it opens with mention of the story of the woman who argued with our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning the zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening one's wife to one's mother) that her husband had pronounced against her.

Among the Aims of the Surah

• To clarify the ruling of Islam on annulling zihar and its expiation (kaffarah), and that it is among the rulings which God rejected, and in which He humbled the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era).

• To mention a number of the misguided acts of the hypocrites (munafiqun): such as their secret conversations in the sight of the believers, their greeting of the Prophet (ﷺ) with other than the greeting with which God greeted him, their allegiance to the Jews, their swearing of false oaths, the prohibition of believers from the manners of the hypocrites, and their being taught the etiquette of the assembly and the etiquette of private conversation with the Prophet (ﷺ).

• To clarify the reality of love and hatred for the sake of God, which is the firmest handhold of faith, and the completion of faith through opposing the enemies of God, and that it is the attribute of those whom God has firmly established faith in their hearts and strengthened with His support, and that they are the successful.

[The Commentary]

God has indeed heard the saying of Khawlah bint Tha'labah, who pleads with you (O Prophet) concerning her husband Aws ibn al-Samit, and concerning what he uttered against her of zihar, which was his saying to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother," that is, in the prohibition of marriage. She was humbly appealing to God Most High to relieve her distress, and God hears your dialogue and your argument. Indeed God is All-Hearing of every saying, All-Seeing of everything, nothing hidden from Him.

Those among you who divorce their wives by likening them to their mothers (saying to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," meaning in the prohibition of marriage) have disobeyed God and contravened the Sharia. Their wives are not in reality their mothers; they are only their wives. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. Indeed, these who liken their wives to their mothers utter a statement that is false and monstrous, whose truth is not known. Truly, God is Pardoning and Forgiving toward whoever has committed some transgressions, so let him make amends for them through sincere repentance.

Those who divorce [i.e., declare their wives unlawful to themselves by ẓihār] from their wives, then retract what they said and intend to resume relations with their wives—then the husband who made the ẓihār must, in that case, pay the expiation for the prohibition, which is freeing a believing slave, male or female, before he has intercourse with the wife he made ẓihār with. That is the ruling of God regarding one who makes ẓihār from his wife, by which you are admonished, O believers, so that you do not fall into ẓihār and false speech, and so that you make expiation if you fall into it, and so that you do not return to it. God is not unaware of anything of your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 4:

Whoever does not find a slave to free, then he must fast two consecutive months before the two of them touch each other. Whoever is unable to fast the two months for a legitimate excuse, then he must feed sixty needy people, those who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, enough to satisfy them. That is what We have explained to you of the rulings of ẓihār, so that you may believe in Allah, follow His Messenger, act upon what Allah has prescribed, and abandon what you used to do in your jāhiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). These rulings mentioned are the commands of Allah and His limits, so do not transgress them. For those who deny them there is a painful punishment.

This is the commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 5.

Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, and disobey their command, will be disgraced and humiliated, just as those nations before them who opposed Allah and His messengers were disgraced. We have sent down clear signs, evident in their proof, indicating that the law of Allah and His limits are true, and for those who deny those signs there is a humiliating punishment in Hell.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 6:

Remember, O Messenger, the Day of Resurrection, the Day when God will bring the dead back to life all together and gather the first and the last generations in one place. He will inform them of what they did, good and bad. God has counted it and recorded it in the Preserved Tablet, and He has kept it recorded against them in their books of deeds, while they had forgotten it. And God is Witness over everything; nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 7:

﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth?﴾ There is no secret conversation among three of His creatures except that He is their fourth, by His knowledge and encompassing; nor among five except that He is their sixth; and no fewer than these numbers mentioned, nor more, except that He is with them by His knowledge, wherever they may be. Nothing about their affairs is hidden from Him. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah, exalted is He, will inform them of what they did, good and bad, and will recompense them for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knower of all things.﴾ Nothing hidden is concealed from Him.

Have you not considered, [O Messenger], those who were forbidden from secret conferring, [yet] they return to what they were forbidden and confer together in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger's command? When they come to you, [O Messenger], they greet you with a greeting other than that with which God has greeted you, saying: "As-sam 'alayk" (meaning: "Death upon you"). And they say among themselves: "Why does God not punish us for what we say to Muhammad, if he were truly a messenger?" Hell is sufficient for them; they will enter it and endure its heat, and it is an evil destination.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: when you speak privately among yourselves, do not speak of what contains sin, or transgression against others, or disobedience to the Messenger's command. Rather, speak of what contains good, obedience and kindness. And fear Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, for to Him alone is your return with all your deeds and words, which He has counted against you, and He will recompense you for them.

The secret conversation of sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger is only from the whispering of Satan, for he is the one who makes it seem appealing and drives people to it, in order to bring grief upon the hearts of the believers. Yet it does not harm the believers in anything except by the permission of God, the Exalted, and His will. And upon God alone let the believers rely, entrusting all their affairs to Him.

O you who have believed, meaning those who affirm Allah and His Messenger and act by His law: when you are told to make room for one another in gatherings, then make room. Allah will widen [His provision] for you in this world and the Hereafter. And when you are told, O believers, to rise from your gatherings for some matter in which there is good for you, then rise. Allah will raise the standing of the sincere believers among you, and He will raise the standing of those who have knowledge by many degrees in reward and in levels of Allah's good pleasure. Allah, the Exalted, is All-Aware of your deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them. In the verse there is an indication of the high standing and virtue of the scholars ('ulama') and the elevation of their ranks.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: when you wish to speak privately with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then before that, give a charity to those in need. That is better for you, because of the reward it contains, and purer for your hearts from sins. But if you do not find anything to give in charity, then there is no blame upon you, for indeed Allah is Forgiving toward His servants, the believers, and Merciful to them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 13:

Are you afraid of poverty if you present charity before your private consultation with the Messenger of Allah? So since you did not do what you were commanded, and Allah has forgiven you and granted you a concession not to do it, then persevere and be constant in establishing the prayer, paying the zakat, and obeying Allah and His Messenger in everything you have been commanded. Allah, glorified is He, is All-Aware of your deeds, and will recompense you for them.

Have you not seen those hypocrites who have taken as allies the Jews and befriended them? The hypocrites are in reality neither of the Muslims nor of the Jews, and they swear falsely that they are Muslims and that you, [O Muhammad], are the Messenger of Allah, while they know that they are liars in what they swear to.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsīr al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 15:

Allah has prepared for these hypocrites a punishment of extreme severity and pain. Indeed, how evil is what they used to do: hypocrisy, and swearing falsely to lies.

The hypocrites have taken their false oaths as a shield for themselves against being killed because of their disbelief, and to prevent the Muslims from fighting them and seizing their wealth. Because of that, they have barred themselves and others from the path of Allah, which is Islam. So for them is a humiliating punishment in the Fire, because of their arrogance toward faith in Allah and His Messenger and their turning others away from His path.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 17:

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah's punishment. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ They will not come out of it. This recompense encompasses everyone who turns others away from the religion of Allah, by their words or their deeds.

On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will raise all the hypocrites from their graves alive. Then they will swear to Him that they were believers, just as they used to swear to you, O believers, in the worldly life. They think that this will benefit them with Allah just as it benefited them with the Muslims in the worldly life. Verily, they are the ones who have reached the extreme of lying, to a degree that no one else has reached.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 19:

Satan has overcome them and taken full control of them, so that they have abandoned the commands of Allah and acting in obedience to Him. Those are the party of Satan and his followers. Indeed, the party of Satan are the losers in this world and in the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 20:

Indeed, those who oppose the command of Allah and His Messenger will be among the humiliated, the defeated, and the disgraced, in this world and in the Hereafter.

God has written in the Preserved Tablet and decreed that victory belongs to Him, to His Book, to His messengers, and to the believing servants. Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful, nothing can overpower Him, and He is Almighty over His creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 58, verse 22:

You, O Messenger, will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and who act upon what Allah has prescribed for them, loving and taking as allies those who oppose Allah and His Messenger and defy their command, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their relatives. Those who take allies for the sake of Allah and show enmity for His sake are the ones in whose hearts Allah has established faith, and has strengthened them with help from Him and support against their enemy in this world. He will admit them in the Hereafter to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein for a lasting period that never ends. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with their Lord for what He has given them of honours and lofty ranks. Those are the party of Allah, and it is they who are the successful, attaining the happiness of this world and the Hereafter.
